notes: Todo, in the Toolbox: to-do lists with a star and a due date on each task. Overdue tasks show in red. Drag a task by its grip to reorder it, or onto another list to move it there. Done tasks drop into a Done section you can clear in one go, and deleting a task or a list can be undone.

BoxConvert, on the home page: drop in any number of files and pick what each one becomes. Pictures to PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF, BMP, a Windows icon (.ico) or a PDF. Videos to MP4, WebM, MKV, MOV or a GIF, or just their sound as MP3, WAV or M4A. Sounds to MP3, WAV, M4A, OGG, Opus or FLAC. Documents to Word, PDF, a web page, Markdown, RTF or text. Spreadsheets to Excel, OpenDocument, CSV or TSV. PDFs to page pictures or text. The new files go next to the originals, or into a folder you pick, and never overwrite anything. Videos and sounds need ffmpeg.

BoxBeat, in the Toolbox: a drum machine with synths. Click or drag across a grid of steps to make a beat, with built-in kick, snare, clap, hats, toms, rim, cowbell, 808, shaker and blip sounds, or any sound file from the audio dump or dropped on a row. Each row has mute, solo, volume, pan, pitch and its own reverb, delay, drive and tone; the beat has tempo (or tap it), swing, humanize, a compressor and 8 to 64 steps. Patterns (A, B, C…) can be chained into a song. Synth rows (Bass, Lead, Pad, Pluck, Keys, Bass guitar, Electric guitar and Acoustic guitar, the guitars strumming chords) are written in a piano roll, in the beat's key and scale. A row can be saved as a line: lines are kept under the Lines tab and can be added to any pattern, adapting to the key. Dice, starting styles, Shift+click for a softer hit, F2 to rename a pattern and Ctrl+Z are there too. Export renders the pattern or the song into the audio dump as an MP3 or WAV, ready in the Music player.

Songs downloaded with BoxTape or BoxKlep now get a genre and a BPM in their tags, shown in the file's details and under the song's title in the music player. The genre is the one the site gives, or else looked up by artist and title from the iTunes song search. The BPM comes from Deezer, or is measured from the song itself when Deezer doesn't have it. A genre with no match is left blank rather than guessed.

The default dark theme is now Dark — charcoal & lavender: plain greys with a bright lavender accent and softer glows, in the app, the code editor and the Markdown preview. The light theme, now Light — lilac & violet, gets the same treatment: soft grey-white with violet and lilac.
Neon dusk is its own theme again: purple, pink and cyan with its glows and its purple logo.
New app icon: the same file-and-prompt logo, now bright white on charcoal with a lavender frame and mark, on the window, the taskbar and the home page.

Music: the full-screen visualizer, the mixer's EQ curve and each song's cover now use the colours of whichever theme is on, instead of always being purple and pink or a random rainbow. Every song still gets its own mix of them.

Every theme now colours the bits that used to stay purple and pink whatever theme was on: the music player's play button, the video and audio trimmer, find highlights, PDF form fields and selection boxes, and the code editor's cursor, selection and find marks.

Music fixes: once a song stopped, the bass bars on the visualizer crept up on their own (the mixer was letting a silent low rumble build up and sending it to the speakers too); and with the mixer open the full-screen player no longer cuts off the top of the song cover.

Box-DocSpitter is now Box-Deckspitter: the name, the BOX//DECKSPITTER header, window titles, menus, dialogs and the launcher (Box-Deckspitter.exe). Shortcuts that pointed at the old launcher are moved over the first time the new version starts. Settings, files and secure notes are untouched.

BoxStudio, on the home page: a screen recorder built around scenes. A scene stacks screens, windows, cameras, pictures, videos, text and colour on a canvas at the resolution you set, each with its own position, size, rotation, crop and flip. Sound from the PC and from one or more microphones is mixed with a volume for each. Global hotkeys start, pause and stop recording and take a still from any program, and Win+Shift+K outlines part of the screen to record just that region. Recordings are saved as MP4, MKV, WebM or MOV in the media dump or a folder you choose.

BoxWave, in the Toolbox: an audio editor. Open a sound or record from a microphone, select part of the waveform and cut, copy, paste, delete, trim, silence, amplify, normalize, fade, reverse or change its speed, all with undo. BoxTunnel's effects can be applied to it. Export as WAV, MP3, FLAC, OGG, Opus or M4A (everything except WAV needs ffmpeg). Sound files have Open in BoxWave on their right-click menu.

BoxTunnel effects: any input, a microphone for example, can run through pitch shift, robot, wobble, echo, reverb, distortion, radio, telephone, megaphone, bass and treble. Presets combine them into voices (Deep voice, Chipmunk, Robot, Alien, Demon, Monster, Radio, Telephone, Megaphone, Cave and Stadium), and a monitor switch plays the processed sound back so you can hear it while you adjust.

Email alerts: BoxMail can watch for new mail containing words you choose or sent by people you choose. Matches add a count to the bell button in the left sidebar, show a pop-up, and send a system notification when the app is in the background. Right-click a message to start watching its sender.

BoxMap, in the Toolbox: a map that works without a connection. A world map with countries, borders, coastlines, lakes and about 7,000 cities is built in. Select an area and download its streets, buildings and place names to keep on this PC, where they can be searched offline. Pins take notes, a ruler measures distances, and street maps show for other places while online. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors; world map from Natural Earth.

BoxLog, in the Toolbox: a log viewer that merges many logs into one timeline. Sources include Windows event logs, log files from Windows and installed programs, and the log folders of Steam, Epic, Unity and Unreal games, Minecraft and common launchers; files and folders can be added by hand. Search by words, phrases, exclusions or regex, filter by level, source and time range (drag across the chart), show the lines around a match, fold repeated lines and save filters. Live mode follows files as they grow, and what's shown can be exported. Logs are only read, never changed.

BoxTerminal, in the Toolbox: a shell inside the app. It runs Windows PowerShell, PowerShell 7 or Command Prompt in a folder you choose, with command history, Tab completion and colour; Ctrl+C stops a running command, and folders in Files have Open in BoxTerminal. It's a command shell rather than a full terminal emulator, so programs that take over the whole screen aren't supported.
The Toolbox has its own order, set by dragging tools up and down and independent of the home page's; a button restores the default.

Video player: opening a video or sound file now plays it in a plain player. The controls hide while it plays, and PgUp/PgDn step through the rest of the folder. It has keyboard shortcuts, speed, loop, picture-in-picture and full screen, and saves frame snapshots to the media dump. Trim and Video editor buttons sit on top. To have files open in the video trimmer as before, change it in Settings › Files.
Right-click a video in the media dump, Files or BoxSpaces and pick Open in the video trimmer.

Pictures: the image viewer (quick crop, rotate, resize) has an Edit in BoxPaint button, and right-clicking a picture in the media dump, Files or BoxSpaces gives Open in the image editor. Settings › Files picks which one opens pictures.
BoxPaint: New image has a 2560×1440 size.

Ask Claude is now the AI assistant, and works with ChatGPT, Gemini, OpenRouter or Perplexity too. Add a key for any of them in Settings › AI assistant and pick which one to use at the top of the panel, along with its model. Perplexity answers list their sources. BoxMail drafts with whichever one is picked.
BoxKlep: next to the download folder, pick Media dump to save downloads straight into the media dump. Stream downloads are turned into MP4 there.

The default theme, neon dusk, has new colours: a blue-hour navy background with sunset coral, orchid and cyan. The code editor and Markdown preview match it, and tool titles and glows follow whichever theme is on.
Win+Shift+Q screenshots over a fullscreen game now let you drag an area or click a window too, instead of saving the whole screen. The game goes back in front afterwards.
Win+Shift+Q screenshots: if one doesn't work, a notice now says why instead of nothing happening, and a screenshot that gets stuck no longer leaves the key dead until a restart.
Win+Shift+Q screenshots of a screen with Windows HDR on come out with the right colours, instead of washed out with blown-out highlights.
Shift+drag works again to carry files out of the media and doc dumps, Files and BoxSpaces (a plain drag still selects several).
Shift+scroll over a tab whose name is cut off scrolls the name, so you can read all of it.
Settings › Files: turn off Show recent files to hide them from the home page, the Recent panel, File › Open recent and quick open.

Screenshots: press Win+Shift+Q anywhere in Windows while Box-DocSpitter is running. Drag to grab an area or click a window, and it's saved straight into the media dump (never the clipboard). When a fullscreen app such as a game is in front, its whole screen is saved at once, without an overlay.

Weather: a button in the top bar (drag it to the right sidebar if you like) shows the conditions and temperature for a place you pick; click it for the next hours and 7 days. Pop it out as a small widget you can drag anywhere, or open the full view from the Toolbox.

Translate: right-click selected text anywhere in the app, the code editor and Browser pages included, to translate it with Google Translate. Read it and close, copy it, or put it in place of the selection.
Browser: drag tabs along the tab strip to reorder them. Pinned tabs stay at the front. The ⋯ menu can send the page to BoxKlep to grab its videos.
Video editor: clips on audio tracks show their waveform. Right-click one to save just the part it plays, at its volume, as an MP3 in the media dump or the audio dump.

Video editor: a video placed on the timeline puts its picture on a video track and its sound on an audio track, linked together. They move, trim, split and delete as one; Ctrl+L unlinks or relinks them.
Video editor: Ctrl+click selects several clips, which move and delete together. With one picture and one sound selected, Ctrl+L links them.
Video editor: Space plays and pauses the video instead of the music, pausing and playing no longer flickers, and a clip whose own sound is muted keeps playing its picture.

Video editor: Volume is a box you can type in or a slider that pops out; the properties panel keeps its place when you click into it; the colour Pick button and the media list's header fit their space.
The tab strip scrolls with the mouse wheel when there are more tabs than fit.
Adding a time zone to the clock finds states, countries and cities by name, and its list scrolls.
The Bloodflame Talons theme is less red: greys and gold trims.
Three more hidden themes.

Your API keys, tokens and email app passwords are now saved encrypted to your Windows account, so a copy of the data folder doesn't give them away. Moved to another PC or Windows account, they need entering again.
Links inside opened Word documents are checked like every other file type's, so a document can't sneak a script link in.
Opening several files at once outside the desktop app opens all of them, not just the first.
Fresh installs are about 130 MB smaller: parts of the code editor and PDF libraries the app never uses are skipped.
A hidden theme got scanlines.
Under the hood: the biggest code files are split into smaller parts. Nothing works differently; it just makes the app easier to keep fixing.
The Tools folder is now the Toolbox, and every tool is in it (the home page's tools in your order, BoxTicker, Quick trim and the pop-out music player), with a filter box.

BoxTicker: Compare lines all follow the same dates. Over long ranges they start together from the first day they all have (a later listing, say) instead of each from its own, and huge % changes shorten (+503K%).
Clicking Music player in the Toolbox again closes it.
In full screen, the full screen button now shows a clear "leave full screen" icon (arrows pointing in) instead of one that looked like a phone, and it always takes you back out.
New Tools folder at the bottom of the left sidebar.

BoxTicker (in Tools): the NASDAQ Composite and the S&P 500, with live prices, today's change, a chart from 1 day to all time with hover read-outs, and a Compare view in % change. Search any ticker or company (stocks worldwide, ETFs, crypto, currencies) to add it as a card of its own. Refreshes every 30 seconds.
Another hidden theme turned up.
A hidden theme stopped dripping.
Image editor: a Crop to selection button in the toolbar.

Image editor: cropping (or making the canvas smaller) no longer throws anything away. What falls outside stays on its layer, hidden, and comes back when you drag the layer with the move tool or make the canvas bigger again. Flipping, rotating and resizing the image keep it too.
Image editor: Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y work right after using a slider or dropdown, and with the text tool's empty typing box open.
Image editor: text goes on a layer of its own (named after what you typed), so you can move, size or hide it separately.
Image editor: moving a selection partly off the picture keeps the part that went off, and Flatten keeps the layers' hidden parts.
Music: songs you add to or delete from the music folder outside the app show up (or disappear) in the player within a few seconds.

Image editor: the move tool is now a transform box. Drag to move, pull the handles to resize, use the dot to rotate, and flip or set an exact size and angle. Works on a whole layer or just the selection.
Image editor: selections can be moved and resized with handles, nudged with the arrow keys, and drawn square with Shift. There's also a new “Select what’s on this layer” option.
Image editor: type text right on the picture, with a font list (your fonts plus every font installed on the PC), a small size dropdown, and bold, italic, underline and alignment.
BoxTape: Spotify playlists over 100 songs now come through in full without a key.
Music player: a BoxTape button next to Add songs.
Improved entertainment feature.
Improved entertainment feature.
PDF editor and PDF from images: Ctrl+wheel zooms, and big image pages open fitted to the window instead of overflowing.
Background image: Settings → Appearance → Choose a picture, or right-click any picture → Set as app background. Sliders for how much theme shows over it and blur. It comes along in the setup export.
Pictures can also be set as your Windows desktop background (right-click, or the Background button in the image editor).
Your fonts: type any Google font's name in Settings → Appearance and click Get. Case, spaces and dashes don't matter, near misses get suggestions, and you can add your own .ttf / .otf.
Improved entertainment feature.
StoragePeek: right-click a box → Hide from storage view. It stays greyed out in “Biggest here”; right-click it there to show it again.
BoxTape finds yt-dlp and ffmpeg after installing them from an admin terminal, or while the app was already open, so the install button no longer says they can’t be found.
BoxTape: missing yt-dlp or ffmpeg? “Install them for me” installs them with winget, ready straight away.
Dropdown lists follow the theme instead of Windows' blue highlight.
The code editor's right-click menu, suggestions and command palette follow the theme too.
README: BoxSwap, BoxTunnel, themes and the newer BoxTape and mixer features are written up.
BoxTape: songs YouTube turns down are tried again automatically, a few seconds apart. Pick how many retries next to “at a time”.
BoxTape: better matching for songs with Japanese, Korean or other non-English titles, and a second search when the first finds nothing close.
BoxTape: YouTube playlists now spot songs already in your audio dump (they start unticked), like Spotify links do.
BoxTape: the note about adding a Spotify key for playlists over 100 songs shows up again.
Music: EQ presets are a dropdown now, and you can save your own (and delete them).
The theme dropdown in Settings follows the theme button.
Tool titles take on the custom theme's colours.
A hidden theme got a lot more… itself.
Settings → Appearance → Interface font: pick the font for the app itself (menus, panels, the home screen), or keep the theme's own.
Settings → Appearance → Animations: turn off hovers, fades and sliding panels; everything still works, it just changes at once.
Custom theme: Gradient background. Pick the colour it fades to and its direction; the window chrome turns to tinted glass over it.
Another hidden theme turned up.
Fixed: in the fullscreen music player, a long library could cover the playlist row under Library/Queue.
Settings → Easter eggs → Hidden themes. A couple of things to find already…

Custom theme: Settings → Appearance → Custom. Pick dark or light, a background, an accent and a highlight (or start from one of nine presets) and the rest of the colours are worked out from them, code editor included.
BoxSpaces: hover a recent space and click × to take it off the list (the folder itself isn't touched).

BoxTunnel: audio lines (BoxAudioLine1, 2, …). Each line mixes any number of inputs (mics or line-in, everything the system is playing, other lines), each with its own volume, mute, level meter and noise gate, through an optional compressor, and plays the mix to any output. Listen lets you hear what's going through a line. Send a line to a virtual audio cable and other apps can use it as a microphone.
BoxVidKlep is now called BoxKlep. A custom name or card position you gave it carries over, and an existing Downloads\BoxVidKlep folder keeps being used.
Setup export no longer carries this PC's pinned tabs, pinned browser tabs or BoxTunnel lines, so importing on another PC doesn't pin the wrong things or point at missing devices.
There's a Box-DocSpitter Discord now: Help → Join the Discord, or the button at the bottom of Settings.
Improved entertainment feature.
Clock in the title bar with alarms, and a calendar whose events can set alarms.
Music: a Music tab, playlists (also in BoxTape), and the song you're playing can show on Discord (never titles of documents or pages).
Paint: zoom up to 6400%, an accuracy slider, and “Image (paint)” in the + menu.

Images: choose the file type (PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF) when making or opening an image, with a warning when transparency or frames would be lost. Image settings: quality, GIF colours and looping, size tools, and seeing or removing hidden info like location.
GIF editor: GIFs open with their frames. Edit each frame or have every stroke add a new one, with a frame strip to reorder, time, duplicate and play them.
PDF: drag images out of a PDF.
BoxSpaces: “+ New BoxSpace” makes a folder (in data\BoxSpaces by default, or anywhere you choose).
Tabs: pin app tabs and browser tabs to keep them small at the left and bring them back next time. All tabs are now one size.
Browser: right-click a page to get its video, or every video on it, with BoxVidKlep.
Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y work everywhere, full-screen mode for the app, and the side bar can be reordered.
Improved entertainment feature.
Tabs: drag a tab up, down or out of the window to open it in a window of its own (unsaved changes go with it). With one tab, dragging it moves the whole window. The windows share one taskbar button.
Browser: the “Logins aren’t kept yet” notice now goes away after the next restart, even if the app is reopened right after closing.
Browser: built-in ad blocker (EasyList, EasyPrivacy and uBlock Origin lists, updated weekly). The shield in the address bar shows what was blocked, turns it off, or allows ads on a site.
Browser: logins are now kept after an in-app restart (updates) too, not only after closing the app.
Setup: if Node.js is missing, the launcher offers to install it with winget.
Improved entertainment feature.
Improved entertainment feature.
Improved entertainment feature.
Improved entertainment feature.
Fixed dragging: moving buttons and tabs between the top bar and the right sidebar works again, and no stray copies are left on screen.
New tool: BoxSwap. Pick a folder (like a game's Mods or Data folder), make profiles of files for it, and hot-swap which profile is in. Profiles live in data/boxswap or a master folder you pick.
BoxSwap never deletes: switches never overwrite, a crash mid-switch is undone next time, and removed profiles go to a .removed folder.
BoxSwap: right-click a folder or profile to set a description, shown at the bottom of its menu.
Right sidebar: drop items anywhere along it (top, middle or bottom) and drag to reorder; items never overlap and the layout is remembered.
Improved entertainment feature.
Tool tabs (browser, BoxMail and the rest) no longer show a meaningless "new" save light in the status bar.
Improved entertainment feature.
The web browser is now in the Tools menu and on the home screen's tools cards too.
Improved entertainment feature.
New: a built-in web browser (globe button on the left). Tabs, find in page, search engine choice and unpacked Chrome extensions; your tabs come back next time.
Right-click a picture, video or sound on a web page to send it to the media dump, or save the whole page to the doc dump as a PDF.
Website logins are kept encrypted on this PC (switched on automatically after the first close). Camera, microphone, location and similar requests ask first.
Links that open other programs, like a site's open-in-app buttons, ask before they do (with an "Always for this site" option).
The browser has its own 10-band equalizer for sound from web pages (browser menu → Equalizer).
Help → README opens the full guide in its own window.
The music player's song list and queue get more room when opened from the top bar.
Improved entertainment feature.
Added entertainment feature.

Box-DocSpitter now starts from Box-DocSpitter.exe instead of the old .vbs script (drag files onto it to open them; on a fresh copy it still sets up the app files first). The app keeps the .exe up to date itself.
The right sidebar folds away when nothing is docked in it, giving the page more room, and slides back out when you drag a button toward it.

New: Secure notes (Tools → Secure notes) — passwords and private notes, encrypted on this PC. Only the app window can open them, the local server never sees them, and a copied file is useless anywhere else.
Secure notes ask for your PIN every time you open them, and lock when you leave the tab, after a few idle minutes, or when Windows locks. After the app restarts, your passphrase is needed.
Your secure key (XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX, made at setup — a sticky note is fine) is asked for every 30 days, and opens your notes on a new PC together with your PIN.

Secure notes: passwords show only while you hold the eye; copied ones clear from the clipboard after 20 s and stay out of Windows clipboard history; the window shows black in screenshots and screen shares while they're open; the last 10 versions are kept. Optional: a key file on a USB stick.
New: an optional PIN lock for the whole app (Settings → Security), with lock after idle, when Windows locks, or Ctrl+Alt+L.
New: export / import your setup (Settings → Your setup): settings, theme, renames and layout, plus your still-encrypted Secure notes, as one .zip. Never the dumps.
Ctrl+right-click files in Files, BoxSpaces, Recent or the dumps to attach them to the email you're writing in BoxMail (Shift+drag works too).
Home: a “clear” button on the recent list.
New home tagline.
Fixed: with the music player in the right sidebar, the song list was squeezed down to about four songs. Now the whole panel scrolls and the list shows every song.

Folders in the media dump and the doc dump: make them with the new-folder button, click one to open it, and use the path at the top (or Mouse 4) to go back up. Drop or Shift+drag files onto a folder to put them in it; things already in the dump are moved, not copied. Works in the sidebar panels, the video editor's dump tab and the dump drawers.

Video editor: clips snap to each other's edges, the playhead and the start, with a guide line where they meet. Press Shift while dragging a clip to place it freely. Files dropped onto the timeline snap too.
Video editor: Shift+click anywhere on the timeline (over clips too) jumps the playhead there, and Shift+drag scrubs. Shift+drag across the preview scrubs through the whole video.
Video editor: 2560 × 1440 (1440p) is now one of the video sizes.
Fixed: a clip's end edge didn't snap when dragging it up to the clip after it.
Fixed: updating from 1.0.11 inside the app said the update changes the app launcher. The launcher is back to how it was, so Settings → Updates can install this one directly.

Fixed: “GitHub is rate-limiting update checks”. Checking and downloading updates no longer goes through GitHub's API (which only allows 60 calls an hour per internet connection, shared by every copy), so it can't run out. With a GitHub token it still uses the API, which allows far more.
The image dump is now the media dump: it keeps videos and sounds as well as pictures (the folder is now media-dump; your old image-dump folder is moved over by itself).
Media dump and Doc dump buttons in the left sidebar, below Recent.

Video editor: a Media dump tab next to the media list. Drag from the dump onto the timeline or the media list, drag a clip or a media file onto the dump to keep a copy, and export straight into the dump.
Shift+drag files from Files, BoxSpaces, Recent or the dumps into another part of the app, like the video editor's timeline. A plain drag still picks several.
Ctrl+right-click a file in Files, BoxSpaces, Recent or a dump to send it to the tool that's open: the video editor adds it to its media list, the document editor and BoxPaint take pictures.
Fixed: in the video editor, a clip didn't move on screen while you dragged it, only when you let go.

New video editor (Tools → Video editor): video and audio tracks, pictures on the timeline (drag the edge to change how long they show), keyframes for position, size, rotation, opacity and volume, chroma key (green screen) with an eyedropper, a properties panel for the selected clip, split, undo, and MP4 export. Projects save as .boxcut.
It's quick: chroma key runs on the graphics card and export overlaps drawing, encoding and saving frames.
Videos the app can't play directly (AVI, WMV, MKV, some MOV) are converted to an editing copy automatically; missing files can be found again from the media list.
The quick trimmer is still there (Tools → Quick trim a video, or open any video file), now with an “Open in video editor” button.
Box-DocSpitter checks for updates when it starts and shows a note in the bottom right if one is out (dismiss it with ×; you can turn the check off in Settings → Updates).
The status bar shows which folder this copy is running from (click it to open the folder).
Fixed: choosing many file types in Settings → Windows failed with “spawn ENAMETOOLONG”.

Settings → Sounds: play, change or reset each UI sound (hover, click, typing, open, close). Pick any audio file; “Default” puts the original back, and “Reset all to default” does them all. Your sounds are kept in data\sounds, so updates don't touch them.

Renaming a tool with F2 on its home card now renames it everywhere: its open tabs, the window title, the tool's own heading, the status bar and the Tools menu. Ctrl+F2 puts the original name back everywhere.
BoxTape searches by words: type a song or artist instead of a link to see the top 20 YouTube results, tick what you want and download.

Paste a list of songs (one per line, or separated by ;), like “Toto - Africa” or just “mr blue sky”: each one is matched to the best YouTube upload and saved to the audio dump. Songs you already have start unticked.
With shuffle on, the Queue tab always shows what's coming: your queued songs, then the shuffled library in the order it will play.
Drag songs in the shuffled list to rearrange it. The shuffle order now stays put (it used to re-roll whenever the song list refreshed); Reshuffle deals a new one.

Drag or flick the chars, claude and clip tabs to the top bar and they become buttons there that drop their panel down; drag them back to the right sidebar any time. Each one remembers where you put it.
Right-click the theme button to go back a theme (left-click still goes forward).
The sound, theme and shortcuts buttons can be dragged or flicked into the right sidebar (and back), styled like the other sidebar tabs.

Drag to select: drag a box over the home page's recent files, the Recent panel, the Files panel or the BoxSpaces tree. Ctrl+click adds one, Shift+click picks a range. Then Del, Enter, or right-click for Open all, Copy paths, Compare (two files) and Delete (Recycle Bin, one question for all).
Drag the home page's Start something and Tools cards into any order you like.
Fixed: two copies of the app (another folder or drive) could open each other's window, settings and music when both were running. Each install now only ever joins its own server.
Fixed: with chars and claude both in the top bar, opening one after the other showed both in the same drop-down, and a docked music player showed through it.

New PB&J theme (after Discord's PB&J gradient): grape jelly fading into warm peanut butter, with the gradient showing through the whole window. Pick it in Settings → Appearance, View, or click the theme button in the top bar to cycle Dark → Light → PB&J.
Copies of the app in different folders or drives no longer get mixed up by Windows: pinning one to the taskbar now always opens that copy. (Re-pin it once after updating.)
The music player remembers the song, the spot in it, the volume and whether it was playing: close the app, restart or update, and it picks up right there.

A queue, separate from the library: right-click a song → Play next / Add to queue, hover it and click +, or drag it onto the Queue tab. Drag queued songs to reorder them. When the queue runs out, the library carries on where it was.
Drag or flick the ♪ button into the right sidebar to dock the player there as its own tab; drag or flick the tab back to the top bar to undock it.
BoxTape: an “Only new songs” button ticks just the songs that aren’t in your audio dump yet.

BoxTape queues downloads: start another playlist while one is downloading and it waits its turn instead of replacing the first. Every download keeps its own progress card, and queued ones can be removed before they start.
Updates from inside the app: Settings → Updates checks GitHub, downloads, checks the new version and installs it on restart. If it doesn't start, the previous version comes back on its own.
Go back to the previous version any time from Settings → Updates (or run “Restore previous version.bat”).
What's new (this window) after every update, and a welcome note the first time the app opens.
Hover a home screen card, the big title, the line under it or the logo and press F2 to change it; Ctrl+F2 puts the original back.
Mouse back / forward buttons move between folders and tabs.
BoxTape takes Spotify playlist, album and song links: each song is matched to the same recording on YouTube and saved as “Artist - Title.mp3”. Songs you already have start unticked.
The music player spots duplicate songs (same file, or “Song (1)”, “Song (Official Video)”…) and can clear the extra copies.
New home screen tagline.
BoxDiff: compare two files side by side — added lines in green, removed in red. Works with text, code, Word, PDF, spreadsheets and pictures.
